summary: 1933 Wisconsin Department of Conservation steel lookout on South Bluff in Wood County, replacing a lower 1931-era tower; listed as standing.

facts.design: Standard square skeleton steel tower with an enclosed cabin on top

events.note: Built by the Wisconsin Department of Conservation to replace a lower, more accessible tower nearby; the 1934 survey also gives 1933
August 1931 Daily Tribune column, quoted on Central US Lookouts, criticized the older tower's site and gave it a height of 75 feet
Registered March 24, 2020; nominated by Jacob Hufnagle

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1931 column gives 75 feet for the older lower tower; the 1934 survey gives 64 feet for the 1933 replacement. Treated as two different towers, so the facts use the 64-foot figure.

notes_for_editor: Build year (1933) and design are corroborated by two sources: NHLR and the 1934 survey text quoted on Central US Lookouts. No staffing, fire, or access sources found; the access and rental questions are open. The 75-foot (1931) and 64-foot (1934) figures are treated as different towers, which is an inference. Search snippets gave TopoQuest 1,115 ft and Wikipedia summit 1,096 ft, but neither page was read, so they are not used. The Komoot and Devil's Nose results describe a different South Bluff in Sauk County and were ignored. A USDA Forest Service PDF named in a search snippet returned 404 and was not used. The Wisconsin Historical Society record HI55878 is the Babcock Ranger Station, not the tower, and was not used.
